results.question: I wrote down 4, so my seen list is [4]. The next number is 7. What should I check before writing it down?
results.reply: Great! You've written down 4, so your seen list is [4]. Now, before adding 7, check if 7 is already in your seen list. Does seen have 7?

results.question: Suppose my seen list contains 1,000 different numbers. To check whether 7 is already there, would an ordinary list need to search through them? How would checking a Set differ? Explain only this comparison, without tracing [4,7,4] again.
results.reply: Yes, with a regular list, checking if 7 is already there might require looking at all 1,000 numbers. In contrast, a Set can usually check in about one try, on average, because it uses a method that quickly finds or confirms the absence of 7.
